overview.headline: How DNA sequencing reads genetic instructions and aids health

keyPoints.point: Sequencing reveals the order of chemical bases that carry genetic information
keyPoints.quote: Sequencing DNA means determining the order of the four chemical building blocks - called "bases" - that make up the DNA molecule.

keyPoints.point: Chemical bases always bond with the same partner to form base pairs in the double helix
keyPoints.quote: In the DNA double helix, the four chemical bases always bond with the same partner to form "base pairs."

keyPoints.point: Researchers compare large stretches of DNA from different individuals quickly and cheaply
keyPoints.quote: Researchers now are able to compare large stretches of DNA - 1 million bases or more - from different individuals quickly and cheaply.

keyPoints.point: Physicians use sequence data to identify particular cancer type for better treatment choices
keyPoints.quote: In cancer, for example, physicians are increasingly able to use sequence data to identify the particular type of cancer a patient has.

keyTerms.gloss: Reading the order of chemical blocks that make up a molecule
keyTerms.quote: DNA sequencing determines the order of the four chemical building blocks - called "bases" - that make up the DNA molecule.

keyTerms.gloss: Chemical units that bond with the same partner to form pairs
keyTerms.quote: In the DNA double helix, the four chemical bases always bond with the same partner to form "base pairs."

keyTerms.gloss: Base that always pairs with thymine in DNA
keyTerms.quote: Adenine (A) always pairs with thymine (T); cytosine (C) always pairs with guanine (G).

keyTerms.gloss: Tiny openings used to sequence DNA with potential advantages
keyTerms.quote: Using nanopores to sequence DNA offers many potential advantages over current methods.
